recap: Amara, Mei e Victor, bloccati dalla neve nel municipio con il budget e il riscaldamento rotto, discussero come gestire il freddo e la mozione sulla chiusura notturna della clinica. Amara impose di evitare fiamme libere per il monossido di carbonio; Mei definì le soglie del pericolo e citò la scarsa evidenza sulla settimana corta; Victor chiese di definire i termini e notò che il timetable decide la partita. Mei raccomandò di votare la versione da dodici ore solo con misurazione indipendente e tramonto della chiusura; Amara trovò in allegato tre i risparmi senza fondi per la misurazione. Redassero una mozione a matita. Resta: mozione scritta a matita, voto rinviato e misurazione da finanziare.

Snowed in at the town hall with a draft budget that would close the night clinic, Amara Okafor, Mei Tanaka-Ruiz and Victor Hale argued past midnight about cold, evidence and the motion itself. Amara ruled out open flames; Mei warned that Victor going quiet would signal dangerous cold. They agreed the vote could not be close-or-not but a defined timetable with a named counterfactual, pre-registered outcomes and sunset on failure, and Amara found annex three itemised savings but funded no measurement. They drafted a pencil motion and set a two o'clock check. A nurse then called Amara: the clinic had its busiest night of the year.

Amara, Mei and Victor, snowed in at the town hall, debated the draft budget that would close the night clinic, with Mei noting the evidence covered mostly professional services and only nine round-the-clock providers, Victor pressing for a defined timetable and counterfactual, and Amara warning that closing nights would push emergency staff into fatigue. They found annex three itemised the savings but funded no measurement, and agreed on a pencil motion to defer the closure, fund two years of independent measurement, pre-register the outcome and sunset on failure. A nurse then called Amara: the clinic had had its busiest night of the year.

Amara raised carbon monoxide and cold-exposure risks; Mei defined the tiers of danger and warned that a quiet Victor would be the warning sign; Victor registered his discontent audibly and called the budget res ipsa loquitur. Amara cited a 38% fatigue increase, Mei noted thin four-day-week evidence (71% professional services, nine round-the-clock providers) and retention falling from 6.1% to 4.3%, while Victor argued the timetable decides the fight. They agreed the vote needed defined hours, a named counterfactual, and measurement outliving the pilot; Mei proposed funding two years of independent measurement and sunsetting closure if numbers failed.

Snowed in at the town hall with a broken heater, Amara, Mei and Victor debated the draft budget that would close the night clinic. Mei cited retention pilots whose response rates decayed to 58%, Amara noted fatigue scores ran 38% higher, and Victor argued the counterfactual — five hours closed versus twelve — was the whole case. Amara found annex three itemised the savings but funded no measurement, so they drafted a pencil motion: defer the closure, fund two years of independent measurement, pre-register the outcome, sunset on failure. After a nurse called about the clinic's busiest night, the census showed sixteen cases per nurse against a December average of ten, with one fewer nurse.

Snowed in at the town hall with a draft budget that would close the night clinic, Amara, Mei and Victor debated staffing evidence, the thin four-day-week pilots and annex three's unfunded measurement line, while Victor kept talking as a hypothermia check. A nurse called Amara: the clinic had its busiest night of the year, sixteen cases per nurse against a December average of ten, with one fewer nurse. Victor then found an unread charter clause, Section 12(c), barring reduced continuous-service staffing below the Health Officers' Schedule ratio. They drafted a pencil motion to defer closure, fund two years of measurement and sunset on failure, and adjourned to sleep.

On the morning of the town's flower festival, Hana's van died outside the shop with three hundred tulips in the back, and she called Kai to her team while saving him the last onigiri. Rin said she couldn't miss her noon deadline, and Takeshi arrived with a clipboard timetable—tulips loaded by 9:15, Rin's deadline by noon—putting Kai on flowers and warming up the second car. Hana and Kai started loading while Takeshi told Rin to eat at the table, not the keyboard. Rin agreed to a four-minute meal, promising to judge the flower arrangements objectively after noon. Hana and Kai set out to build the stall, aiming to beat Takeshi's 10:40 schedule.

On the morning of the town's flower festival, Hana's van died outside the shop with three hundred tulips in the back, and Takeshi took charge with his clipboard, scheduling the tulips loaded by 9:15 and Rin's deadline by noon. Rin ate at the table in under four minutes, then coded while Hana and Kai built the stall with Takeshi's help. The festival committee then called needing twice as many sunflowers by two o'clock; Takeshi added a sunflower column to the clipboard, assigning himself the sunflower run at 11:10 and Rin as navigator after her noon deadline. Things stand with Rin finishing her compile at 11:58 and reporting for navigator duty two minutes early, right on schedule.
